headline: 45th BCS: 1,702 candidates appointed after 10-month wait
summary: The Ministry of Public Administration issued the gazette late Wednesday, directing the new recruits to join their respective offices by November 1.
details: The government has appointed 1,702 candidates from the 45th Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) examination, ending a wait of more than 10 months.
The Ministry of Public Administration issued the appointment gazette on Wednesday night, October 14, with recruits ordered to join their ministries or divisions on November 1.
While the Public Service Commission (PSC) had recommended 1,807 candidates last November, the final gazette excludes 105 people without providing an explanation.
Among the appointees, 266 are assigned to the administration cadre, 71 to the police cadre, and nine to the foreign affairs cadre.
The new officers will join in Grade 9 under the National Pay Scale 2026, with a basic salary ranging from Tk 44,000 to Tk 1,05,900.
Appointees must report to their designated offices on November 1; failure to do so will result in the cancellation of their appointment.
The recruits will serve a two-year probationary period, which may be extended by another two years, and must undergo foundation and specialized training.
They are also required to submit declarations of assets owned by themselves and their family members.

headline: 20 Bangladeshis killed in Russia-Ukraine war after being trafficked
summary: Victims were lured with high-paying construction jobs but forced into the Russian military and used as 'bait' in drone strikes.
details: At least 30 Bangladeshis were trafficked to Russia with promises of high-paying jobs, only to be forced into the Russian military and sent to the front lines of the Russia-Ukraine war.
The Special Response Battalion (SRB) reported that 20 of them have died, including 17 who were killed in drone strikes on their first day of deployment.
Investigators believe the victims were used as 'bait' to reveal enemy positions, having received only 21 days of training and no prior combat experience.
The victims reportedly paid an average of Tk 10 lakh each to recruiting agencies, including Jabal-e-Noor, RS International, and TS Group, for promised construction work.
Of the 10 survivors, two injured men have returned to Bangladesh, one of whom suffered lower-body paralysis after dragging himself four kilometres to safety.
The SRB has arrested two men, including the alleged mastermind Mizanur Rahman, and is searching for other syndicate members and foreign accomplices.
A separate investigation by Fortify Rights and Truth Hounds found that at least 104 Bangladeshis had been recruited into the Russian military by February 2026, with 34 killed.
caption:
Promised high-paying jobs, but used as 'bait' in a war zone. 20 Bangladeshis killed after being trafficked to Russia.

At least 30 Bangladeshis were trafficked to Russia with promises of high-paying jobs, only to be forced into the Russian military and sent to the front lines of the Russia-Ukraine war.

The Special Response Battalion (SRB) reported that 20 of them have died, including 17 who were killed in drone strikes on their first day of deployment.

Investigators believe the victims were used as 'bait' to reveal enemy positions, having received only 21 days of training and no prior combat experience.

The victims reportedly paid an average of Tk 10 lakh each to recruiting agencies, including Jabal-e-Noor, RS International, and TS Group, for promised construction work.

Of the 10 survivors, two injured men have returned to Bangladesh, one of whom suffered lower-body paralysis after dragging himself four kilometres to safety.

The SRB has arrested two men, including the alleged mastermind Mizanur Rahman, and is searching for other syndicate members and foreign accomplices.

A separate investigation by Fortify Rights and Truth Hounds found that at least 104 Bangladeshis had been recruited into the Russian military by February 2026, with 34 killed.
